---
title: "Codespaces"
---

A GitHub Codespace is VS Code in your browser,
already set up with R, Quarto,
the tidyverse, `tidymodels` and `medicaldata`.
All you need is a GitHub account.

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/chendaniely/MEDI-504A-2026W1-biostats)

This Codespace uses the same setup as the
[HDSx course book](https://ehsanx.github.io/HDSx/),
whose pages walk through each step with screenshots:

- [Opening Your First Codespace](https://ehsanx.github.io/HDSx/weeks/week02-modern-workflows/workflows03-open-codespace.html)
- [The Setup](https://ehsanx.github.io/HDSx/weeks/week03-r-with-ai/r01-setup.html):
  R, Quarto and GitHub Copilot in your Codespace
- [Reopening a Codespace](https://ehsanx.github.io/HDSx/weeks/week02-modern-workflows/workflows04-reopen-codespace.html)
- [Stop Your Codespace](https://ehsanx.github.io/HDSx/weeks/week02-modern-workflows/workflows10-stop-codespace.html)

## Check that it works

Once the Codespace is ready,
open `example.qmd` and render it.
It loads the course packages,
draws three charts,
and fits a small logistic regression.
The rendered files go in the `_site/` folder:
click `_site/example.html` to open the page.
It should match the [Example](example.qmd) page on this website.
